questions.question: What is a common challenge faced during the data digitization process?

options.C: High costs of digitization and ensuring data accuracy during conversion

questions.explanation: Digitization projects are repeatedly documented as expensive (scanning, OCR, indexing, quality-control manpower) and error-prone (garbled OCR, missing fields, duplicate/legacy records needing cleansing before they can be trusted) — this matches the syllabus point on 'Data quality, validation and cleansing'. A is backwards (digitisation is meant to reduce, not need, physical storage), B and D describe symptoms rather than the actual bottleneck of the conversion process itself.

questions.sub: What data digitization means and why it precedes service delivery
questions.question: A fire broke out in XYZ office, all important documents were lost/damaged. What option will be the best for ABC office in order to safeguard their documents?
questions.explanation: Digitization converts records into electronic form that can be backed up and stored off-site, so a fire destroys no information. Fire equipment, fire-resistant rooms and photocopies all still leave a single physical location holding the only copies.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a stakeholder for Digitize India Platform?
questions.explanation: The Digitize India Platform is built on crowdsourcing, so its stakeholders are the user organizations submitting scanned documents, the digital contributors who transcribe snippets, and the platform operators. The conventional data entry operator is precisely the role the crowdsourced model replaces.

questions.question: A district office wants to deliver a certificate service online, but the records that must be checked before issuing the certificate exist only as paper registers. Why is digitization of those legacy registers a prerequisite for the online service?

options.A: Because the online workflow cannot verify an application against a record that the software cannot read or search
options.B: Because the law does not allow paper registers to be retained once a service is offered online
options.C: Because scanning reduces the physical storage cost of the registers
options.D: Because digitized registers automatically satisfy the department's data protection obligations

questions.explanation: An online service is only end-to-end if the back-end verification step is also electronic; as long as the authoritative record is a paper register, a clerk still has to pull the volume by hand and the service is merely a digital front-end. Reduced storage cost is a side benefit, not the reason the service depends on digitization.

questions.question: In a records digitization programme, what does a 'day-forward' approach mean?

options.A: All existing records are converted first, and only then is the new system switched on
options.B: Only records created from the cut-over date onward are captured electronically, with the older backlog handled as a separate exercise
options.C: Records are re-scanned every day to keep a fresh copy
options.D: Only the records of the current financial year are retained and the rest are destroyed

questions.explanation: Day-forward capture starts the electronic record from a chosen date so that new business is born digital immediately, while the historical backlog is converted on its own timeline or on demand. Converting everything before go-live is the opposite, backlog-first approach, and it usually delays the project far longer.

questions.question: During digitization of departmental files, why is metadata captured for each scanned document in addition to the page images?

options.A: It compresses the image so the file occupies less disk space
options.B: It encrypts the document so that only authorised officers can open it
options.C: It supplies the indexing attributes — such as file number, subject, date and office — by which the document can later be searched and retrieved
options.D: It guarantees that the scan is a legally admissible copy of the original

questions.explanation: A repository of un-indexed page images is effectively unsearchable, so capture of descriptive metadata is what turns a pile of scans into a retrievable record set. Compression and encryption are separate processing steps and neither depends on metadata.

questions.question: Two departments each digitize their records but define the same field differently — one stores a citizen's name as a single field, the other as first and last name, and their date formats differ. What is the main consequence for e-governance?

options.A: The scanned images will be of unequal resolution
options.B: The two datasets cannot be reliably exchanged or matched without a costly reconciliation, which is exactly what common data standards exist to prevent
options.C: Each department will need a separate scanner model
options.D: The records will lose their legal validity in both departments

questions.explanation: Agreed data standards fix the structure, format and meaning of shared elements so that data captured in one department is intelligible to another; without them every inter-departmental exchange needs bespoke mapping and produces matching errors. Image resolution and scanner choice are capture concerns unrelated to field definitions.

questions.question: What does applying OCR to a scanned page add that plain scanning alone does not provide?

options.A: A machine-readable text layer that makes the content searchable
options.B: A higher optical resolution for the scanned image
options.C: A digital signature attesting to the document's authenticity
options.D: Automatic removal of duplicate pages from the batch

questions.explanation: A scan produces only a picture of the page; optical character recognition interprets the shapes as characters and stores the recognised text, so full-text search and data extraction become possible. Resolution is fixed at capture time and is not changed by OCR, and signing is an entirely separate step.

questions.question: Which capability is characteristic of a document management system rather than of an ordinary shared network folder?

options.A: Allowing several users to open the same file at once
options.C: Maintaining version history and a check-in/check-out and access-control regime over each document
options.D: Providing a larger amount of disk space

questions.explanation: A document management system adds controlled custody over the document lifecycle — versioning, check-in/check-out to prevent conflicting edits, retention rules and per-document permissions — on top of mere storage. A shared folder gives directories and space but no managed version history.

questions.question: Before the production cut-over of a legacy-to-new-system data migration, why is a trial or dry-run migration into a test environment normally carried out?

options.A: To increase the transfer speed of the final migration run
options.B: To let the vendor bill for an additional phase of work
options.C: To make the legacy system read-only
options.D: To surface transformation errors, rejected records and reconciliation mismatches while there is still time to correct them

questions.explanation: A dry run exercises the full extract-transform-load path on real data and produces the error and reconciliation reports that reveal bad mappings and dirty source records before go-live. It is a rehearsal for correctness, not a performance tuning exercise.

questions.question: After migrating records from a legacy application to a new one, which check most directly establishes that no data was silently lost or altered in transit?

options.A: Confirming that the new application's screens load without errors
options.B: Reconciling record counts and control totals of key fields between source and target, plus sample-level field comparison
options.C: Confirming that the migration job finished without an operating-system error
options.D: Asking users whether the new system feels faster than the old one

questions.explanation: Counts and control totals compared on both sides, backed by row-level sampling, are what actually prove completeness and fidelity of a migration. A job that exits cleanly can still have dropped rejected rows to a log, which is precisely how silent migration loss happens.
